title: Regular Expression Matching Variant
statement:
You are given a text `s` and a pattern `p`. Decide whether the pattern matches the **entire** text.

The pattern is made of lowercase letters, `.` and `*`, and supports two special symbols:

- `.` matches any single character.
- `*` matches **zero or more** copies of the element right before it (that element is a lowercase letter or `.`). For example `a*` matches `""`, `a`, `aa`, ...; and `.*` matches any string, including the empty one.

The match must cover all of `s`, not just a part of it. The pattern is always well formed: `*` is never the first character of `p`, and it always follows a letter or a `.` (never another `*`).

Print `true` if the whole text is matched by the pattern, otherwise `false`.

**Follow-up:** the interviewer asked how the solution would change "at scale", for example when the same pattern must be tested against millions of texts, or when texts and patterns are too long to compare in quadratic time. Discuss it; the tests only check the single-pair problem.
input_format:
The first line contains the text `s`.
The second line contains the pattern `p`.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
p consists of lowercase English letters, `.` and `*`, and is well formed as described above

examples.explanation: Read the pattern as `m`, `i`, `s*`, `i`, `s*`, `i`, `p*`, `.`. They match "m", "i", "ss", "i", "ss", "i", "pp" and "i", which uses up the whole text.
`c*` matches zero characters, `a*` matches "aa" and `b` matches "b", so the whole text is matched.
`.*` can take "ab" and `c` takes "c", but then "d" is left over. The pattern must cover the entire text, and `.*` followed by `c` forces the text to end in `c`, so the answer is false.

hints: Define a state (i, j): does the first i characters of `s` match the first j characters of `p`? Think about what the last pattern character can be.
If `p[j-1]` is `*`, there are two choices: use zero copies of the element before it (look at (i, j-2)), or let that element absorb `s[i-1]` when they agree (look at (i-1, j)).
Initialise the empty-text row carefully: a prefix of the pattern matches the empty text only if it is made of pairs like `a*`. Each row depends only on the previous one, so two rows are enough.
